### aa-missing-value

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [aa-airspace-activation-times](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#aa-airspace-activation-times)
- Automatic fix: no

An AA command must have a value.

An AA command without a value has no meaning. Write an interval, a weekday command, an exception or NONE. Remove the AA command if the airspace is always active.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA
```

### aa-invalid-syntax

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [aa-airspace-activation-times](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#aa-airspace-activation-times)
- Automatic fix: --fix writes "-" in place of other dashes (for example the en dash "–"), removes the spaces around "/", and writes "/" in place of "-" between two times ("07:00Z/15:00Z" in place of "07:00Z-15:00Z"). It does not change other problems.

The AA command must have one of the forms of the specification.

There are four forms of AA command:

AA StartDateTime/EndDateTime (an interval)
AA [Weekdays] StartTime/EndTime [StartDate/EndDate] (a weekday command)
AA EXCEPT Date or AA EXCEPT StartDate/EndDate (an exception)
AA NONE

This rule reports a command that matches none of these forms, for example a command with extra text, a missing "/" or an ICAO code such as H24 or HJ. A reader that cannot parse an AA command ignores all AA commands of the airspace.

Correct:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
AA SR/SS
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 2026-07-04 08:00Z/2026-07-04 16:00Z
AA HJ
```

### aa-invalid-date

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [time](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#time)
- Automatic fix: no

A date in an AA command must be a valid ISO 8601 date.

Dates in AA commands are ISO 8601 dates in the form YYYY-MM-DD. The date must exist in the calendar: 2026-02-30 is not valid. In date ranges and in AA EXCEPT, write only the date, without a time.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
AA EXCEPT 2026-12-25
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
AA EXCEPT 2026-02-30
```

### aa-invalid-time

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [time](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#time)
- Automatic fix: no

A time in an AA command must be a valid ISO 8601 time.

Times in AA commands are ISO 8601 times of day in UTC, for example 09:00Z. The hour is 00 to 23 and the minutes are 00 to 59. Write two digits for each value. An interval needs a date and a time on both sides, for example 2026-07-04T08:00Z. A weekday command uses times without a date.

Correct:

```
AA MON 09:00Z/11:30Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON 9:00Z/25:00Z
```

### aa-invalid-duration

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1
- Specification: [aa-airspace-activation-times](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/v2.1.5/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#aa-airspace-activation-times)
- Automatic fix: no

In version 2.1, a duration in an interval must be a valid ISO 8601 duration.

Version 2.1 of the specification allows the ISO 8601 time interval format. This format allows a start and a duration, for example 2026-07-04T08:00Z/PT8H. The duration has the form PnYnMnDTnHnMnS, for example PT8H (8 hours), P1D (1 day) or P1DT12H. Only the last value can have a decimal fraction. The alternative format of ISO 8601, for example P0000-00-01T00:00:00, is also read. A duration must be shorter than 10 000 years, and the interval must stay between the years 0000 and 9999.

Version 3.0 does not allow durations. For version 3.0 files, the rule aa-interval-form-not-allowed reports every duration. Write the interval as StartDateTime/EndDateTime.

Correct:

```
*VERSION: 2.1
...
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
*VERSION: 2.1
...
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/P8H
```

### aa-time-missing-z

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [time](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#time)
- Automatic fix: no

Every time of day must end with Z (UTC).

All times in OpenAir are UTC. Write Z after every time of day. In ISO 8601, a time without Z is local time, and OpenAir does not support local time. If the source publishes local time, convert it to UTC first.

Correct:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00/2026-07-04T16:00
```

### aa-time-zone-not-z

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [time](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#time)
- Automatic fix: --fix writes Z in place of UTC, UT, ZULU and GMT, and in place of an offset of 0 (for example +00:00). It does not change another offset (for example +01:00) or a local time (LT or a zone name such as CET), because then the time itself must change.

Times must use Z, not a time zone offset or a zone name.

OpenAir supports only UTC, written as Z. Time zone offsets such as +01:00 and names such as UTC, GMT, LT or CET are not allowed. Convert the time to UTC and write Z. For UTC and GMT, only write Z in place of the name.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 06:00Z/14:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-FRI 08:00+02:00/16:00+02:00
```

### aa-time-24-as-start

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [time](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#time)
- Automatic fix: no

24:00Z is allowed only as an end time.

24:00Z means the end of the day. It can only be an end time. As a start time, write 00:00Z (in an interval: 00:00Z of the next day).

Correct:

```
AA 2026-07-05T00:00Z/2026-07-05T06:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 2026-07-04T24:00Z/2026-07-05T06:00Z
```

### aa-value-form-not-allowed

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 3.0
- Specification: [time](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#time)
- Automatic fix: --fix writes the same date or time in an allowed form, for example "2026-07-04T08:00Z" in place of "20260704T0800Z". It does not change a value with a decimal fraction.

Dates and times must use one of the allowed forms.

The specification allows only these forms of dates and times:

DateTime: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, for example 2026-07-04T08:00Z
Date: YYYY-MM-DD, for example 2026-12-25
Time: hh:mmZ or hh:mm:ssZ, for example 09:00Z

Other ISO 8601 forms are not allowed: the basic format without separators (20260704T0800Z), week dates (2026-W27-6), ordinal dates (2026-185), decimal fractions (08:00:00.5Z), a time with only the hour (08Z) and a time with the letter T in front (T08:00Z). The message shows the value in an allowed form.

Version 2.1 of the specification allows every ISO 8601 form. For version 2.1 files, the rule aa-value-form-not-allowed-v21 reports these forms as a warning.

Correct:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00:30Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 20260704T0800Z/20260704T1600Z
```

### aa-value-form-not-allowed-v21

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1
- Specification: [time](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#time)
- Automatic fix: --fix writes the same date or time in an allowed form, for example "2026-07-04T08:00Z" in place of "20260704T0800Z". It does not change a value with a decimal fraction.

In version 2.1, dates and times should use a form that version 3.0 allows.

Version 2.1 of the specification says that times use the ISO 8601 format. It does not limit the forms. Version 3.0 allows only some forms. The specification allows only these forms of dates and times:

DateTime: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, for example 2026-07-04T08:00Z
Date: YYYY-MM-DD, for example 2026-12-25
Time: hh:mmZ or hh:mm:ssZ, for example 09:00Z

Other ISO 8601 forms are not allowed: the basic format without separators (20260704T0800Z), week dates (2026-W27-6), ordinal dates (2026-185), decimal fractions (08:00:00.5Z), a time with only the hour (08Z) and a time with the letter T in front (T08:00Z). The message shows the value in an allowed form.

A file of version 2.1 with other forms is valid, but it cannot become a version 3.0 file without changes. Readers of version 3.0 do not have to read the other forms. For version 3.0 files, the rule aa-value-form-not-allowed reports these forms as an error.

Correct:

```
*VERSION: 2.1
...
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
*VERSION: 2.1
...
AA 20260704T0800Z/20260704T1600Z
```

### aa-none-not-allowed

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [aa-airspace-activation-times](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#aa-airspace-activation-times)
- Automatic fix: no

NONE is allowed only where the specification allows it.

NONE is allowed in AA NONE, on one side of an interval (AA NONE/EndDateTime, AA StartDateTime/NONE) and on one side of the date range of a weekday command. It is not allowed in the time window of a weekday command and not in AA EXCEPT.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z 2026-04-01/NONE
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/NONE
```

### aa-none-none

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [interval-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#interval-activation)
- Automatic fix: --fix writes "AA NONE".

AA NONE/NONE is not allowed. Write AA NONE.

An older draft of the specification used AA NONE/NONE for an airspace without known activation times. The specification replaced it with AA NONE. Readers can understand NONE/NONE in different ways: as "never active until known" or as "always active".

Correct:

```
AA NONE
```

Incorrect:

```
AA NONE/NONE
```

### aa-interval-end-before-start

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [interval-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#interval-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

The end of an interval must be after its start.

An interval AA command defines one activation interval from StartDateTime to EndDateTime. If the end is before the start, or the same as the start, the interval is empty. This is usually a typing error in the date or the time.

Correct:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 2026-07-04T16:00Z/2026-07-04T08:00Z
```

### aa-interval-form-not-allowed

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 3.0
- Specification: [interval-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#interval-activation)
- Automatic fix: --fix writes the same interval as StartDateTime/EndDateTime, for example "2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z" in place of "2026-07-04T08:00Z/PT8H".

Intervals must have the form StartDateTime/EndDateTime.

An interval AA command must have the form StartDateTime/EndDateTime. NONE can replace the start or the end (AA StartDateTime/NONE, AA NONE/EndDateTime). Other ISO 8601 interval forms are not allowed: a start and a duration (2026-07-04T08:00Z/PT8H), a duration and an end (PT8H/2026-07-04T16:00Z), an end with only the time (2026-07-04T08:00Z/16:00Z) and an end without the year or the month (2026-07-04T08:00Z/07-05T16:00Z). When the values are valid, the message shows the interval in the allowed form.

Version 2.1 of the specification allows every ISO 8601 interval form. For version 2.1 files, the rule aa-interval-form-not-allowed-v21 reports these forms as a warning.

Correct:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/PT8H
```

### aa-interval-form-not-allowed-v21

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1
- Specification: [interval-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#interval-activation)
- Automatic fix: --fix writes the same interval as StartDateTime/EndDateTime, for example "2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z" in place of "2026-07-04T08:00Z/PT8H".

In version 2.1, intervals should have the form StartDateTime/EndDateTime.

Version 2.1 of the specification says that AA uses the ISO 8601 time interval format. It does not limit the forms. Version 3.0 allows only one form. An interval AA command must have the form StartDateTime/EndDateTime. NONE can replace the start or the end (AA StartDateTime/NONE, AA NONE/EndDateTime). Other ISO 8601 interval forms are not allowed: a start and a duration (2026-07-04T08:00Z/PT8H), a duration and an end (PT8H/2026-07-04T16:00Z), an end with only the time (2026-07-04T08:00Z/16:00Z) and an end without the year or the month (2026-07-04T08:00Z/07-05T16:00Z). When the values are valid, the message shows the interval in the allowed form.

A file of version 2.1 with other forms is valid, but it cannot become a version 3.0 file without changes. Readers of version 3.0 do not have to read the other forms. For version 3.0 files, the rule aa-interval-form-not-allowed reports these forms as an error.

Correct:

```
*VERSION: 2.1
...
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
*VERSION: 2.1
...
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/PT8H
```

### aa-intervals-overlap

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [interval-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#interval-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

Activation intervals should not overlap.

Two interval AA commands of one airspace should not cover the same time. Overlapping intervals are often a typing error. If the intervals are correct, merge them into one interval.

Correct:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T12:00Z
AA 2026-07-04T14:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T12:00Z
AA 2026-07-04T10:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

### aa-intervals-adjacent

- Severity: **info**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [interval-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#interval-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

Adjacent intervals can be merged into one interval.

If one interval ends exactly when another interval starts, the two intervals can be one AA command. The specification allows separate commands, but encourages maintainers to merge them.

Correct:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T12:00Z
AA 2026-07-04T12:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

### aa-intervals-not-sorted

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 3.0
- Specification: [interval-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#interval-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

Interval AA commands should be sorted by their start time.

When an airspace has more than one interval, the intervals should be sorted from the earliest to the latest start time. Version 3.0 recommends this order, and readers must accept any order.

Version 2.1 of the specification required this order. For files that are checked as version 2.1, the rule aa-intervals-not-sorted-v21 reports it as an error.

Correct:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T12:00Z
AA 2026-07-05T08:00Z/2026-07-05T12:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 2026-07-05T08:00Z/2026-07-05T12:00Z
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T12:00Z
```

### aa-intervals-not-sorted-v21

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1
- Specification: [aa-airspace-activation-times](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/v2.1.5/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#aa-airspace-activation-times)
- Automatic fix: no

In version 2.1, interval AA commands must be sorted by their start time.

Version 2.1 of the specification says that the intervals of an airspace must be sorted from the earliest to the latest start time. A reader of version 2.1 can depend on this order. So in a file that is checked as version 2.1, intervals in another order are an error.

Version 3.0 only recommends this order. For version 3.0 files, the rule aa-intervals-not-sorted reports it as a warning.

Correct:

```
*VERSION: 2.1
...
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T12:00Z
AA 2026-07-05T08:00Z/2026-07-05T12:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
*VERSION: 2.1
...
AA 2026-07-05T08:00Z/2026-07-05T12:00Z
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T12:00Z
```

### aa-weekday-invalid-name

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [weekday-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#weekday-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

Weekdays must be MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT or SUN.

A weekday AA command can start with a list of weekdays. Use only the three-letter names MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT and SUN. A list uses commas (MON,WED,FRI) and a range uses a dash (MON-FRI). Other names, such as MO or MONDAY, and codes such as PH (public holidays) are not allowed.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MO-FR 07:00Z/15:00Z
```

### aa-weekday-range-same-day

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [weekday-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#weekday-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

The first and the last day of a weekday range must be different.

A range such as MON-MON is not allowed, because it is not clear: it can mean one day or every day. For one day, write only the day (MON). For every day, leave the weekdays out. A reader treats a command with such a range as a command it cannot parse, and then ignores all AA commands of the airspace.

Correct:

```
AA MON 09:00Z/11:30Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-MON 09:00Z/11:30Z
```

### aa-weekday-list-has-spaces

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [weekday-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#weekday-activation)
- Automatic fix: --fix removes the spaces when the list has a "," or "-" at each space, for example "MON,WED,FRI" in place of "MON, WED, FRI". It does not change "MON FRI", because it can mean MON,FRI or MON-FRI.

The list of weekdays must not contain spaces.

Write the weekdays as one word, without spaces: MON,WED,FRI or MON-FRI,SUN. A reader uses the spaces to find the parts of the command, so it cannot parse a list with spaces.

Correct:

```
AA MON,WED,FRI 09:00Z/11:30Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON, WED, FRI 09:00Z/11:30Z
```

### aa-weekday-duplicate-day

- Severity: **info**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [weekday-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#weekday-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

A weekday should be in the list only once.

A day that is in the list more than once does not change the meaning, but it can be a typing error. For example MON-FRI,WED has Wednesday two times.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI,SUN 07:00Z/15:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-FRI,WED 07:00Z/15:00Z
```

### aa-weekday-every-day

- Severity: **info**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [weekday-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#weekday-activation)
- Automatic fix: --fix removes the weekdays.

Leave the weekdays out when the command is for every day.

If the weekdays are left out, the schedule applies to every day. A list with all seven days, such as MON-SUN, means the same. The shorter form is easier to read.

Correct:

```
AA 06:00Z/20:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-SUN 06:00Z/20:00Z
```

### aa-date-range-end-before-start

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [weekday-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#weekday-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

The end date of a weekday date range must not be before the start date.

The date range StartDate/EndDate of a weekday command includes both dates. The end date can be the same as the start date, but not earlier. If it is earlier, the command never applies.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 06:00Z/14:00Z 2026-03-29/2026-10-24
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-FRI 06:00Z/14:00Z 2026-10-24/2026-03-29
```

### aa-date-range-none-none

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [weekday-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#weekday-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

A weekday date range should not be NONE/NONE.

NONE is for one open end of a date range, for example 2026-04-01/NONE. The specification does not show NONE/NONE. For a schedule with no time limit, leave the date range out. Some readers may not accept NONE on both sides.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z NONE/NONE
```

### aa-weekday-never-active

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [weekday-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#weekday-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

A weekday command should have at least one window in its date range.

A weekday command with a date range has no effect when none of its weekdays is in the date range, or when AA EXCEPT commands remove every day of it. This is usually a mistake in the weekdays or in the dates.

For a window without a sun event, the weekdays and the dates are UTC days. For a window with a sun event, the specification says that they mean the local day at the airspace. openair-lint uses the local solar day (see aa-sun-event-missing-day). In polar regions, a window with a sun event can be not active on every day of its date range, for example SR/SS during the polar night. This rule reports that case too, when the date range is not longer than four years.

Correct:

```
AA SAT,SUN 08:00Z/18:00Z 2026-07-04/2026-07-05
```

Incorrect:

```
AA SAT,SUN 08:00Z/18:00Z 2026-07-06/2026-07-10
```

### aa-except-end-before-start

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [exceptions](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#exceptions)
- Automatic fix: no

The end date of an AA EXCEPT range must not be before the start date.

AA EXCEPT StartDate/EndDate removes the weekday windows of the dates from StartDate to EndDate. Both dates are included. For a window without a sun event, the dates are the UTC days on which the window starts. For a window with a sun event, they mean the local day at the airspace. If the end date is before the start date, the command removes nothing.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
AA EXCEPT 2026-12-31/2027-01-01
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
AA EXCEPT 2027-01-01/2026-12-31
```

### aa-except-without-weekday

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [exceptions](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#exceptions)
- Automatic fix: no

AA EXCEPT can be used only in an airspace with a weekday AA command.

AA EXCEPT removes windows of weekday AA commands. It does not change interval commands. An airspace that has AA EXCEPT must have at least one weekday AA command.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
AA EXCEPT 2026-12-25
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 2026-12-24T07:00Z/2026-12-26T15:00Z
AA EXCEPT 2026-12-25
```

### aa-except-no-effect

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [exceptions](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#exceptions)
- Automatic fix: no

An AA EXCEPT command should remove at least one weekday window.

AA EXCEPT removes the weekday windows of its dates. If no weekday command has a window on these dates, the exception has no effect. For example, the date is outside the date ranges of all weekday commands, or the date is a Saturday and the weekday commands are for MON-FRI only.

For a window without a sun event, the date is the UTC day on which the window starts. For a window with a sun event, the specification says that the date means the local day at the airspace. openair-lint uses the local solar day (see aa-sun-event-missing-day). In both cases, the date removes the window of the day with this date.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
AA EXCEPT 2026-12-25
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
AA EXCEPT 2026-12-26
```

### aa-sun-event-not-allowed

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [sun-events](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#sun-events)
- Automatic fix: no

Sun events are allowed only in the time window of a weekday command.

The sun events SR, SS, BCMT and EECT can replace a Time value in a weekday AA command. They cannot be used in interval commands, in dates or in AA EXCEPT.

Correct:

```
AA SAT,SUN SR/SS 2026-07-04/2026-07-05
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/SS
```

### aa-sun-event-order-changes

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [weekday-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#weekday-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

The order of a fixed time and a sun event must be the same on every day of the schedule.

If the end time of a weekday window is earlier than or equal to the start time, the window ends on the next local solar day. With a sun event, the client compares the calculated times. So 06:00Z/SR ends on the same day when sunrise is after 06:00 UTC, but on the next day when sunrise is before 06:00 UTC. The specification says that the writer must check that the order is correct on every day of the schedule. It uses 06:00Z/SR as an example of a wrong command.

The specification says that the weekday and the date of a window with a sun event mean the local day at the airspace. It does not say how to calculate the local day. openair-lint uses the local solar day, from 00:00 to 24:00 local solar time. Local solar time is UTC plus the longitude of the centre of the airspace divided by 15, in hours (east is positive). The centre is the middle of the box around the airspace. openair-lint calculates the sun event that happens on this local solar day. A fixed time in the same window, for example 07:00Z in 07:00Z/SS, is a UTC time inside this local solar day.

This rule checks windows with one sun event and one fixed time. It reports the command when the window ends on the same local solar day on some days and on the next local solar day on other days. Days on which the sun event does not happen (polar regions) are not compared.

openair-lint calculates the sun events at the centre of the airspace for every scheduled local solar day. Without a date range, it checks the four years 2026 to 2029. With an open end, it checks four years from the start date, but not before 2026. It checks at most four years. The sun times repeat almost exactly every four years. Days removed by AA EXCEPT are not checked.

To fix it, split the command with date ranges, or use a different time.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/SS 2026-04-01/2026-09-30
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 06:00Z/SR
```

### aa-sun-event-near-fixed-time

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [weekday-activation](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#weekday-activation)
- Automatic fix: no

A fixed time and a sun event of one window should not be less than 5 minutes apart.

If the end time of a weekday window is earlier than or equal to the start time, the window ends on the next local solar day. The specification says that different calculation methods can give results that differ by a few minutes. If a fixed time and a sun event are very close on some day, readers can disagree on the order. Then one reader ends the window on the same day, and another reader ends it on the next day.

The specification does not give a limit. openair-lint uses 5 minutes. It reports the first scheduled day on which the fixed time and the sun event are less than 5 minutes apart. It does not report a command that aa-sun-event-order-changes already reports.

openair-lint calculates the sun events at the centre of the airspace for every scheduled local solar day. Without a date range, it checks the four years 2026 to 2029. With an open end, it checks four years from the start date, but not before 2026. It checks at most four years. The sun times repeat almost exactly every four years. Days removed by AA EXCEPT are not checked.

To fix it, use a fixed time that is further from the sun event, or split the command with date ranges.

Correct:

```
AA 02:00Z/SR 2026-06-20/2026-06-22
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 03:12Z/SR 2026-06-20/2026-06-22
```

### aa-sun-event-fixed-start-near-day-start

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [sun-events](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#sun-events)
- Automatic fix: no

In a window with a sun event, a fixed start time should not be less than 2 minutes from the start of the local solar day.

The specification says that the weekday and the date of a window with a sun event mean the local day at the airspace. It does not say how to calculate the local day. openair-lint uses the local solar day, from 00:00 to 24:00 local solar time. Local solar time is UTC plus the longitude of the centre of the airspace divided by 15, in hours (east is positive). The centre is the middle of the box around the airspace. openair-lint calculates the sun event that happens on this local solar day. A fixed time in the same window, for example 07:00Z in 07:00Z/SS, is a UTC time inside this local solar day.

The local solar day starts at 00:00Z minus 4 minutes for each degree of east longitude. For example, at 15° E it starts at 23:00Z of the UTC day before. A fixed start time at this moment is at the start of one local solar day and at the end of the day before. Readers calculate the centre of the airspace in slightly different ways, for example for arcs. A small difference in the longitude can put the start on a different UTC day. Then the window moves by one day. In 23:00Z/SS at 15° E, the window starts at 23:00Z on the UTC day before the local solar day, or it starts at 23:00Z on the same UTC day and ends at sunset on the next day.

A fixed end time at the start of the local solar day is not a problem: both readings give the same end.

The specification does not have this rule. The limit of 2 minutes (0.5° of longitude) is a choice of openair-lint.

To fix it, use a start time that is at least 2 minutes from the start of the local solar day, or use a window without a sun event.

Correct:

```
AA 05:00Z/SS             * an airspace at 15° E
V X=46:00:00N 015:00:00E
DC 5
```

Incorrect:

```
AA 23:00Z/SS             * an airspace at 15° E
V X=46:00:00N 015:00:00E
DC 5
```

### aa-sun-event-near-date-line

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [sun-events](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#sun-events)
- Automatic fix: no

The centre of an airspace with a sun event should not be less than 0.5° from longitude 180°.

The specification says that the weekday and the date of a window with a sun event mean the local day at the airspace. It does not say how to calculate the local day. openair-lint uses the local solar day, from 00:00 to 24:00 local solar time. Local solar time is UTC plus the longitude of the centre of the airspace divided by 15, in hours (east is positive). The centre is the middle of the box around the airspace. openair-lint calculates the sun event that happens on this local solar day. A fixed time in the same window, for example 07:00Z in 07:00Z/SS, is a UTC time inside this local solar day.

At longitude 180° the local solar day changes by 24 hours. At 179.9° E the local solar day 4 July starts at about 12:00Z on 3 July. At 179.9° W it starts at about 12:00Z on 4 July. Readers calculate the centre of the airspace in slightly different ways, for example for arcs or for an airspace that crosses longitude 180°. Near longitude 180°, a small difference in the longitude can move every window with a sun event by one day. The specification does not say what to do in this case.

openair-lint reports every weekday command with a sun event when the centre of the airspace is less than 0.5° from longitude 180°. 0.5° is 2 minutes of local solar time. In this case aa-sun-event-fixed-start-near-day-start does not report the command again.

To fix it, use fixed UTC times in place of the sun events. Use date ranges if the times change during the year.

Correct:

```
AA SAT 18:30Z/05:40Z     * an airspace at 180°
V X=17:00:00S 180:00:00E
DC 5
```

Incorrect:

```
AA SAT SR/SS             * an airspace at 180°
V X=17:00:00S 180:00:00E
DC 5
```

### aa-sun-event-missing-day

- Severity: **info**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [sun-events](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#sun-events)
- Automatic fix: no

A sun event does not happen on some days of the schedule.

In polar regions a sun event does not happen on some days. For example, the sun does not set in the summer, and it does not rise in the winter. The specification says: on these days, AA SR/SS means active for the whole day in summer and not active in winter. AA SS/SR is the opposite.

The specification says that the weekday and the date of a window with a sun event mean the local day at the airspace. It does not say how to calculate the local day. openair-lint uses the local solar day, from 00:00 to 24:00 local solar time. Local solar time is UTC plus the longitude of the centre of the airspace divided by 15, in hours (east is positive). The centre is the middle of the box around the airspace. openair-lint calculates the sun event that happens on this local solar day. A fixed time in the same window, for example 07:00Z in 07:00Z/SS, is a UTC time inside this local solar day.

The specification does not say more about polar regions. For the other cases openair-lint uses these choices:

The position of the sun: for SR and SS, the centre of the sun is 0°50′ below the horizon (the usual value for the radius of the sun and the refraction). For BCMT and EECT, it is 6° below the horizon.
From a morning event to an evening event (SR/SS, BCMT/EECT): if the sun stays above the horizon of the event all day, the window is active for the whole local solar day. If it stays below, the window is not active.
From an evening event to a morning event (SS/SR, EECT/BCMT): if the sun stays above the horizon of the event all day, the window is not active. If it stays below, the window is active for the whole local solar day. If the evening event happens but the morning event of the same day does not, the window ends at the morning event of the next day.
A sun event and a fixed time (07:00Z/SS): if the sun stays above the horizon of the event all day, a missing morning event is the start of the local solar day, and a missing evening event is the end of the local solar day. If it stays below, the window is not active.

This rule tells you on which days this happens and what the window means on these days, so that you can check that this is what you want.

openair-lint calculates the sun events at the centre of the airspace for every scheduled local solar day. Without a date range, it checks the four years 2026 to 2029. With an open end, it checks four years from the start date, but not before 2026. It checks at most four years. The sun times repeat almost exactly every four years. Days removed by AA EXCEPT are not checked.

Correct:

```
AA SR/SS                 * an airspace at 46° N
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DC 5
```

Incorrect:

```
AA SR/SS                 * an airspace at 70° N
V X=70:00:00N 020:00:00E
DC 5
```

### aa-sun-event-no-position

- Severity: **info**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [sun-events](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#sun-events)
- Automatic fix: no

Sun events need the position of the airspace.

A client calculates a sun event at the centre of the airspace. openair-lint could not find any valid point in the geometry of this airspace, so it could not check the sun events. Fix the geometry first.

Correct:

```
AA SR/SS
V X=46:03:00N 014:30:00E
DC 5
```

Incorrect:

```
AA SR/SS
DC 5
```

### aa-none-combined

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [combining-aa-commands](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#combining-aa-commands)
- Automatic fix: no

AA NONE cannot be combined with other AA commands.

AA NONE means that no activation times are known. It overrides all other activation times. If an airspace has AA NONE, it must not have any other AA command. Readers can understand the combination in different ways.

Correct:

```
AA NONE
```

Incorrect:

```
AA NONE
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

### aa-duplicate

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [combining-aa-commands](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#combining-aa-commands)
- Automatic fix: --fix removes the second command when its line has no comment.

An airspace should not have the same AA command twice.

Two AA commands with the same meaning in one airspace are usually a copy error. Remove one of them. The check compares the meaning, so 2026-07-04T08:00Z and 20260704T0800Z are the same.

Correct:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
AA MON-FRI 07:00Z/15:00Z
```

### aa-order-not-recommended

- Severity: **info**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [combining-aa-commands](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#combining-aa-commands)
- Automatic fix: no

AA commands should be in the recommended order.

The recommended order of the AA commands of one airspace is:

1. Interval commands, sorted by StartDateTime.
2. Weekday commands, sorted by StartDate. Commands without a date range come first.
3. AA EXCEPT commands, sorted by Date or StartDate.

This order makes the file easier to read. It does not change the meaning. The order of the intervals among themselves is checked by aa-intervals-not-sorted (version 3.0) and aa-intervals-not-sorted-v21 (version 2.1).

Correct:

```
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
AA MON-FRI 06:00Z/14:00Z 2026-03-29/2026-10-24
AA EXCEPT 2026-05-01
```

Incorrect:

```
AA EXCEPT 2026-05-01
AA MON-FRI 06:00Z/14:00Z 2026-03-29/2026-10-24
AA 2026-07-04T08:00Z/2026-07-04T16:00Z
```

### aa-needs-version-3

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1
- Specification: [aa-commands-a-reader-does-not-understand](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#aa-commands-a-reader-does-not-understand)
- Automatic fix: no

Weekday commands, AA EXCEPT and sun events need version 3.0.

Weekday AA commands, AA EXCEPT and the sun events SR, SS, BCMT and EECT are new in version 3.0. A reader of version 2.1 cannot parse them. It then ignores all AA commands of the airspace and shows the airspace as always active.

Write "*VERSION: 3.0" in the header, or use only interval commands.

Correct:

```
*VERSION: 2.1
...
AA 2026-07-06T07:00Z/2026-07-06T15:00Z
```

Incorrect:

```
*VERSION: 2.1
...
AA MON 07:00Z/15:00Z
```

### coordinate-syntax

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [geographic-position](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#geographic-position)
- Automatic fix: no

A coordinate must have the form DD:MM:SS[N|S] DDD:MM:SS[E|W] or DD:MM.mmm[N|S] DDD:MM.mmm[E|W].

A coordinate has a latitude and a longitude, separated by a space. Each part has degrees and minutes, separated by ":". DMS adds the seconds after another ":". DDM writes the minutes with decimals. Each part ends with its letter: N or S for the latitude, E or W for the longitude.

This rule reports text that is not a coordinate, for example a missing number, a missing longitude or too many ":" parts. A reader cannot read such a point. It can skip the point or the whole airspace.

Correct:

```
DP 45:40:30N 014:18:20E
DP 45:40.500N 014:18.333E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 45:40:30N
DP 45::30N 014:18:20E
DP 45:40:30:10N 014:18:20E
```

### coordinate-hemisphere-invalid

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [geographic-position](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#geographic-position)
- Automatic fix: no

The latitude must end with N or S, and the longitude with E or W.

The letter after each part of a coordinate gives the hemisphere. The latitude ends with N (north) or S (south). The longitude ends with E (east) or W (west). Without the letter, or with the wrong letter, the position is not known. Numbers with a sign (for example -45:40:30) are not allowed.

Correct:

```
DP 45:40:30N 014:18:20E
DP 33:51:35S 151:12:40E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 45:40:30 014:18:20
DP 45:40:30E 014:18:20N
DP 45:40:30Q 014:18:20E
```

### coordinate-out-of-range

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [geographic-position](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#geographic-position)
- Automatic fix: no

The latitude must be at most 90 degrees, the longitude at most 180 degrees, and minutes and seconds must be less than 60.

A latitude greater than 90 degrees or a longitude greater than 180 degrees is not a position on the earth. Minutes and seconds go from 0 to 59. The value 60 is not allowed.

Such a value is probably a typing error. Find the correct value in the source data, for example in the AIP, and correct it by hand. openair-lint does not change the value, because it cannot know the correct one.

Correct:

```
DP 41:08:50N 019:06:00E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 41:08:60N 019:06:00E
DP 91:00:00N 019:06:00E
```

### coordinate-decimal-degrees

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [geographic-position](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#geographic-position)
- Automatic fix: no

Decimal degrees are not allowed. Use DMS or DDM.

The specification allows two notations for coordinates: degrees, minutes and seconds (DMS, 45:40:30N) and degrees and decimal minutes (DDM, 45:40.500N). Decimal degrees (45.675N) are not allowed. Many readers cannot read them.

This rule also reports a part with whole degrees only (46N). It has no minutes.

Correct:

```
DP 45:40:30N 014:18:20E
DP 45:40.500N 014:18.333E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 45.675N 14.305556E
DP 46N 014E
```

### coordinate-trailing-text

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [geographic-position](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#geographic-position)
- Automatic fix: no

A coordinate must not have more text after the longitude.

After the longitude and its letter (E or W), only a comment is allowed. A comment starts with "*". Other text after the coordinate is not part of the format. Readers can fail on it, or read it in different ways.

Correct:

```
DP 45:40:30N 014:18:20E * near the river
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 45:40:30N 014:18:20E near the river
```

### coordinate-space-between-parts

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [geographic-position](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#geographic-position)
- Automatic fix: --fix writes one space between the latitude and the longitude, and one space in place of two or more blanks before the letter N, S, E or W.

Write one space between the latitude and the longitude, and at most one space before the letter N, S, E or W.

The latitude and the longitude are separated by one space character. A missing space, two or more spaces, or a tab are not the specified format.

Between the number and its letter N, S, E or W, you can write no space or one space. Both forms are valid and have the same meaning: 45:40:30N and 45:40:30 N. Two or more spaces, or a tab, are not the specified format.

Correct:

```
DP 45:40:30N 014:18:20E
DP 45:40:30 N 014:18:20 E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 45:40:30N014:18:20E
DP 45:40:30N   014:18:20E
DP 45:40:30  N 014:18:20  E
```

### coordinate-digit-count

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [geographic-position](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#geographic-position)
- Automatic fix: --fix adds the leading zeros, and removes extra zeros at the start ("45" in place of "045"). It does not change a part with too many digits that are not zeros.

Degrees, minutes and seconds should have a fixed number of digits.

The latitude has 2 digits for the degrees (DD), the longitude has 3 digits (DDD). Minutes and seconds have 2 digits (MM, SS). Add leading zeros where needed: write 014:08:05E, not 14:8:5E. Fixed widths make the files easy to read and to compare.

This is a warning, not an error. The colons separate the parts, so the meaning is clear, and readers must accept fewer digits.

Correct:

```
DP 45:40:30N 014:08:05E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 45:40:30N 14:8:5E
```

### coordinate-decimal-seconds

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [geographic-position](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#geographic-position)
- Automatic fix: no

DMS seconds should be whole numbers.

The DMS format is DD:MM:SS with whole seconds. One second is about 30 m. If you need more precision, use DDM (DD:MM.mmm). Three decimals of a minute are about 2 m.

Correct:

```
DP 45:40:30N 014:18:20E
DP 45:40.508N 014:18.342E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 45:40:30.5N 014:18:20.5E
```

### coordinate-mixed-notation

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [geographic-position](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#geographic-position)
- Automatic fix: no

The parts of a coordinate, and the two points of a DB arc, should use the same notation.

The specification says: use a consistent format for each command or data point. Write both parts of a coordinate in DMS (45:40:30N 014:18:20E) or both in DDM (45:40.500N 014:18.333E).

A DB command has two points. Write both points in the same notation.

Correct:

```
DP 45:40:30N 014:18:20E
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DB 46:10:00N 014:00:00E, 46:00:00N 014:14:24E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 45:40:30N 014:18.333E
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DB 46:10:00N 014:00:00E, 46:00.000N 014:14.400E
```

### coordinate-file-mixed-notation

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [dp-polygon-point](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#dp-polygon-point)
- Automatic fix: no

Use one notation (DMS or DDM) for all coordinates of a file.

The specification says: do not mix DMS and DDM notations. Stick to one definition throughout the file.

This rule finds the notation of the first coordinate in the file. It reports the first coordinate that uses the other notation. It reports only one problem per file. Coordinates with decimal degrees are reported by the rule coordinate-decimal-degrees. A coordinate that mixes both notations, and a DB command whose two points use different notations, are reported by the rule coordinate-mixed-notation.

Correct:

```
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00.000N 014:10.000E
```

### geometry-polygon-too-few-points

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [dp-polygon-point](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#dp-polygon-point)
- Automatic fix: no

A polygon must have at least 3 different points that are not on one line.

An airspace is an area. Its boundary needs at least 3 different points, and the points must not all be on one line. Otherwise the airspace has no area and readers cannot draw it.

The closing point (the copy of the first point at the end) does not count as a different point. An airspace with a DC circle is not checked by this rule.

Correct:

```
AC D
AN Example CTR
AH 4500 FT AMSL
AL GND
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
```

Incorrect:

```
AC D
AN Example CTR
AH 4500 FT AMSL
AL GND
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
```

### geometry-polygon-not-closed

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [dp-polygon-point](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#dp-polygon-point)
- Automatic fix: --fix adds the first point again as the last point ("DP" and the same coordinates). It does this only when the polygon starts with a DP point that is written correctly, and when the gap is 0.1 NM or more. A smaller gap is probably a typing error in a coordinate, which the user must check.

The last point of a polygon should be the same as the first point.

The specification says that polygons are expected to be closed: the last point is the same as the first point. Most readers close an open polygon, but the file is clearer when the polygon is closed. The message gives the distance between the last and the first point. A large distance can mean that a point is missing.

The rule checks polygons that have at least one DP point and that start and end with a DP or DB point. The specification gives the "closed" rule in the DP section, so a boundary without DP points (for example two DB arcs) is not checked. A boundary that starts or ends with a DA arc is not checked either, because the end of the arc is calculated.

Correct:

```
AC D
AN Example CTR
AH 4500 FT AMSL
AL GND
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
```

Incorrect:

```
AC D
AN Example CTR
AH 4500 FT AMSL
AL GND
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:00:00E
```

### dp-duplicate-point

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [dp-polygon-point](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#dp-polygon-point)
- Automatic fix: --fix removes the second point when both points have exactly the same position and the second line has no comment.

Two DP commands in a row should not have the same point.

A DP point that is the same as the DP point before it adds nothing to the polygon. It is often a copy error. Remove one of the two points.

The closing point of a polygon is not a duplicate, because it is not next to the first point.

Correct:

```
AC D
AN Example CTR
AH 4500 FT AMSL
AL GND
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:10:00E
```

### geometry-polygon-counter-clockwise

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [dp-polygon-point](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#dp-polygon-point)
- Automatic fix: --fix writes the DP points in the opposite order. It does this only for a closed polygon of DP points without comments between or after the points. A boundary with arcs (DA, DB) or V commands is not changed, because the arcs would need other changes too.

The points of a polygon are expected in clockwise order.

The specification says that polygon points are expected to be mapped clockwise and closed. Most readers draw the airspace correctly in both directions, but a program can use the direction, for example to find the inside of the airspace. Write the points in clockwise order. If you write the file with a program, change the program.

The rule checks the whole boundary, also arcs. It does not check a boundary that crosses itself, because such a boundary has no single direction.

Correct:

```
AC D
AN Example CTR
AH 4500 FT AMSL
AL GND
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:00:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:10:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
```

### geometry-polygon-self-intersection

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [d-geometric-definitions](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#d-geometric-definitions)
- Automatic fix: no

The boundary of an airspace should not cross itself.

The specification says: the boundary of an airspace should not cross itself. A boundary that crosses itself does not define a clear area. Readers can fill it in different ways, so pilots can see different airspaces. The cause is often a point in the wrong order, a wrong coordinate, or an arc with the wrong direction (V D=+ or V D=-).

The boundary can touch itself. For example, a ring-shaped airspace is drawn as one boundary: the outer ring, a connecting line to the inner ring, the inner ring in the opposite direction, and the same connecting line back. This rule does not report it. Only a real crossing is reported: the boundary goes from one side of itself to the other side. Edges that only touch, a line that is used twice, and a point that the boundary passes twice without crossing are not reported.

The message gives the position of the first crossing and the two edges that cross. Arcs are checked as many short edges. A crossing that makes only a very thin loop (less than 25 m wide on average) is not reported. Such loops come from rounded coordinates or from an arc that touches a straight edge, and they are not visible on a map. An airspace with a DC circle or a DY airway is not checked.

Correct:

```
AC D
AN Example CTR
AH 4500 FT AMSL
AL GND
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:10:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:00:00E
DP 45:55:00N 014:10:00E
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
```

### geometry-center-missing

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [v-variable-assignment](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#v-variable-assignment)
- Automatic fix: no

DA, DB and DC need a "V X=" centre before them in the same airspace.

The commands DA, DB and DC draw arcs and circles around a centre. The centre is set with "V X=<point>". The specification says that the V command must be declared before the command that uses it.

The V values are reset at every AC. At the start of each airspace, X has no value. So each airspace must set its own centre. A centre from an earlier airspace is not used.

Correct:

```
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DC 2.00
```

Incorrect:

```
DC 2.00
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
```

### da-wrong-format

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [da-arc-between-start-and-end-bearing](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#da-arc-between-start-and-end-bearing)
- Automatic fix: no

DA needs three numbers separated by commas: radius, start bearing and end bearing.

The format is "DA Radius, Start Angle, End Angle". The radius is in nautical miles, without a unit. The bearings are in degrees, from 0 to 360. Use a point (.) for decimals.

Correct:

```
V X=39:13:00N 118:13:00W
DA 10, 270, 290
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=39:13:00N 118:13:00W
DA 10 270 290
DA 10NM, 270, 290
DA 2,5, 270, 290
```

### da-radius-not-positive

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [da-arc-between-start-and-end-bearing](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#da-arc-between-start-and-end-bearing)
- Automatic fix: no

The radius of a DA arc must be greater than 0.

The radius is the distance from the centre to the arc, in nautical miles. A radius of 0 or less does not draw an arc.

Correct:

```
V X=39:13:00N 118:13:00W
DA 10, 270, 290
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=39:13:00N 118:13:00W
DA 0, 270, 290
```

### da-bearing-out-of-range

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [da-arc-between-start-and-end-bearing](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#da-arc-between-start-and-end-bearing)
- Automatic fix: no

The bearings of a DA arc must be from 0 to 360 degrees.

The start and end bearings are true bearings in degrees, from 0 to 360. 0 and 360 are both north. Negative values and values above 360 are not allowed.

Correct:

```
V X=39:13:00N 118:13:00W
DA 10, 270, 290
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=39:13:00N 118:13:00W
DA 10, -90, 380
```

### da-combined-with-dp

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [da-arc-between-start-and-end-bearing](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#da-arc-between-start-and-end-bearing)
- Automatic fix: no

Avoid DA arcs in an airspace that also has DP points.

The specification says: combining DA arcs with DP points can result in inconsistencies in how the airspace is displayed. Avoid DA if possible.

The start and end of a DA arc are calculated from the centre, the radius and the bearings. Readers calculate them in slightly different ways, so the arc does not meet the DP points exactly. Use a DB arc in its place. DB gives the start and end points of the arc directly. This rule reports the first DA of each airspace that also has DP points.

Correct:

```
DP 39:23:00N 118:13:00W
V X=39:13:00N 118:13:00W
DB 39:23:00N 118:13:00W, 39:13:00N 118:00:06W
DP 39:03:00N 118:13:00W
```

Incorrect:

```
DP 39:23:00N 118:13:00W
V X=39:13:00N 118:13:00W
DA 10, 0, 90
DP 39:03:00N 118:13:00W
```

### da-not-recommended

- Severity: **info**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [da-arc-between-start-and-end-bearing](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#da-arc-between-start-and-end-bearing)
- Automatic fix: no

Avoid DA arcs if possible. DB arcs are clearer.

The specification says: avoid using DA if possible. The start and end points of a DA arc are calculated from the centre, the radius and the bearings, and readers calculate them in slightly different ways. A DB arc gives the start and end points directly.

DA is allowed. The sentence "Avoid using DA if possible" is in a note about DA arcs combined with DP points. That case is reported by da-combined-with-dp (a warning). In an airspace without DP points, the problem of the note (arcs that do not meet the points) does not happen. For this reason this rule is info, not a warning. It reports the first DA of each airspace without DP points.

Correct:

```
V X=39:13:00N 118:13:00W
DB 39:23:00N 118:13:00W, 39:13:00N 118:00:06W
DB 39:13:00N 118:00:06W, 39:23:00N 118:13:00W
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=39:13:00N 118:13:00W
DA 10, 0, 90
DA 10, 90, 0
```

### db-wrong-format

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [db-arc-between-start-and-end-point](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#db-arc-between-start-and-end-point)
- Automatic fix: no

DB needs two points separated by a comma.

The format is "DB Point 1, Point 2". The arc goes from the first point to the second point around the "V X=" centre. Write a comma between the two points.

Correct:

```
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DB 46:10:00N 014:00:00E, 46:00:00N 014:14:24E
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DB 46:10:00N 014:00:00E 46:00:00N 014:14:24E
```

### db-radius-mismatch

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 3.0
- Specification: [db-arc-between-start-and-end-point](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#db-arc-between-start-and-end-point)
- Automatic fix: no

Both points of a DB arc must have the same distance from the centre.

A DB arc is given by a centre and two points. This is more information than an arc needs: the specification says that the arc is over-defined. If the two points have different distances from the centre, readers draw the arc in different ways. Some use the distance of the first point, some use the average, and some draw a spiral. The specification says: "Both points must be at the same distance from the centre."

This rule reports an arc when the two distances differ by more than 0.1 NM plus 1 % of the radius. Smaller differences come from rounding the coordinates and are not reported. Check the centre and the two points.

Correct:

```
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DB 46:10:00N 014:00:00E, 46:00:00N 014:14:24E
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DB 46:10:00N 014:00:00E, 46:00:00N 014:20:00E
```

### db-radius-mismatch-v21

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1
- Specification: [db-arc-between-start-and-end-point](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/v2.1.5/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#db-arc-between-start-and-end-point)
- Automatic fix: no

Both points of a DB arc should have the same distance from the centre (version 2.1).

A DB arc is given by a centre and two points. This is more information than an arc needs: the specification says that the arc is over-defined. If the two points have different distances from the centre, readers draw the arc in different ways. Some use the distance of the first point, some use the average, and some draw a spiral. Version 2.1 only asks to calculate the centre carefully. Version 3.0 says that both points must be at the same distance from the centre, so this is an error in version 3.0.

This rule reports an arc when the two distances differ by more than 0.1 NM plus 1 % of the radius. Smaller differences come from rounding the coordinates and are not reported. Check the centre and the two points.

Correct:

```
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DB 46:10:00N 014:00:00E, 46:00:00N 014:14:24E
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DB 46:10:00N 014:00:00E, 46:00:00N 014:20:00E
```

### dc-wrong-format

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [dc-circular-area](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#dc-circular-area)
- Automatic fix: no

DC needs one number: the radius in nautical miles.

The format is "DC Radius". The radius is in nautical miles, without a unit. Use a point (.) for decimals.

Correct:

```
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DC 2.00
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DC 2 NM
```

### dc-radius-not-positive

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [dc-circular-area](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#dc-circular-area)
- Automatic fix: no

The radius of a DC circle must be greater than 0.

A circle with a radius of 0 or less has no area.

Correct:

```
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DC 2.00
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DC 0
```

### dc-mixed-with-other-geometry

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 3.0
- Specification: [dc-circular-area](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#dc-circular-area)
- Automatic fix: no

A DC circle must be the only geometry command of its airspace.

DC defines a circular area. The circle is the whole airspace. The specification says: DC must be the only geometry command of its airspace. Do not combine it with DP, DA, DB, DY or a second DC. Readers handle such a combination in different ways, and often draw a wrong shape.

Write one airspace for each circle. If the area is a part of a circle, use DP points with DB arcs.

V commands are not geometry commands. "V X=" and "V D=" before the DC are allowed.

Correct:

```
AC UNC
AY Q
AN PARA Example
AH FL100
AL GND
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DC 2.00
```

Incorrect:

```
AC UNC
AY Q
AN PARA Example
AH FL100
AL GND
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DC 2.00
DP 50:40:00N 007:56:42E
```

### dc-mixed-with-other-geometry-v21

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1
- Specification: [dc-circular-area](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#dc-circular-area)
- Automatic fix: no

A DC circle should be the only geometry command of its airspace (version 2.1).

DC defines a circular area. The circle is the whole airspace. The specification says: DC must be the only geometry command of its airspace. Do not combine it with DP, DA, DB, DY or a second DC. Readers handle such a combination in different ways, and often draw a wrong shape.

Write one airspace for each circle. If the area is a part of a circle, use DP points with DB arcs.

V commands are not geometry commands. "V X=" and "V D=" before the DC are allowed.

The version 2.1 text does not have this rule. Version 3.0 has it, and there it is an error (dc-mixed-with-other-geometry). A reader of a 2.1 file has the same problem, so openair-lint reports a warning in version 2.1 files.

Correct:

```
AC UNC
AY Q
AN PARA Example
AH FL100
AL GND
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DC 2.00
```

Incorrect:

```
AC UNC
AY Q
AN PARA Example
AH FL100
AL GND
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DC 2.00
DP 50:40:00N 007:56:42E
```

### dy-deprecated

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [dy-airway-segment](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#dy-airway-segment)
- Automatic fix: no

DY airway segments are not recommended. Use DP points.

DY is part of the original WinPilot format. The specification does not recommend it: consecutive DY segments do not join cleanly into one continuous airway. Draw the airway as a polygon with DP points.

This rule reports the first DY of each airspace.

Correct:

```
AC D
AY AWY
AN Example airway
AH FL195
AL FL95
DP 46:02:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:02:00N 015:00:00E
DP 45:58:00N 015:00:00E
DP 45:58:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:02:00N 014:00:00E
```

Incorrect:

```
AC D
AY AWY
AN Example airway
AH FL195
AL FL95
V W=4
DY 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DY 46:00:00N 015:00:00E
```

### dy-width-missing

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [v-variable-assignment](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#v-variable-assignment)
- Automatic fix: no

DY needs a "V W=" airway width before it in the same airspace.

The format is "DY Point". Each DY is one point of an airway. The width of the airway is set by a preceding "V W=<number>" command, in nautical miles. The specification says that the V command must be declared before the command that uses it. Without a width, readers cannot draw the airway.

The V values are reset at every AC. At the start of each airspace, W has no value. So each airspace must set its own width. A width from an earlier airspace is not used.

This rule reports the first DY of each airspace that has no width before it.

Correct:

```
V W=4
DY 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DY 46:00:00N 015:00:00E
```

Incorrect:

```
DY 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DY 46:00:00N 015:00:00E
```

### v-wrong-format

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [v-variable-assignment](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#v-variable-assignment)
- Automatic fix: no

V must have the form "V Name=Value".

The V command sets a variable. The format is "V Command=Value": a name, the "=" sign, and a value. The names are X (centre), D (direction) and W (airway width).

Correct:

```
V X=39:29.9N 119:46.1W
V D=-
```

Incorrect:

```
V X 39:29.9N 119:46.1W
V D=
```

### v-space-around-equals

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [v-variable-assignment](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#v-variable-assignment)
- Automatic fix: --fix removes the blanks: "V X=..." in place of "V X = ...".

Write "V Name=Value" without blanks around "=".

The format of the V command is "V Command=Value". The specification writes the name, the "=" sign and the value without blanks between them. Many readers accept blanks around "=", but it is not the specified format and a strict reader can fail.

Correct:

```
V X=39:29.9N 119:46.1W
V D=-
```

Incorrect:

```
V X = 39:29.9N 119:46.1W
V D= -
```

### v-unknown-variable

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [v-variable-assignment](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#v-variable-assignment)
- Automatic fix: no

The V variable must be X, D or W.

The specification defines three variables: X sets the centre for DA, DB and DC, D sets the direction of arcs, and W sets the width of an airway. Readers ignore other names, or read them in different ways.

Correct:

```
V X=39:29.9N 119:46.1W
```

Incorrect:

```
V C=39:29.9N 119:46.1W
```

### v-invalid-direction

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [v-variable-assignment](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#v-variable-assignment)
- Automatic fix: no

V D= must be "+" (clockwise) or "-" (counter-clockwise).

V D= sets the direction of the DA and DB arcs that follow. "+" is clockwise, which is also the default. "-" is counter-clockwise. Other values are not allowed.

Correct:

```
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
V D=-
DA 5, 200, 270
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=46:00:00N 014:00:00E
V D=CCW
DA 5, 200, 270
```

### v-invalid-width

- Severity: **error**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [v-variable-assignment](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#v-variable-assignment)
- Automatic fix: no

V W= must be a number greater than 0.

V W= sets the width of an airway in nautical miles, without a unit. The width must be greater than 0.

Correct:

```
V W=4
```

Incorrect:

```
V W=4NM
V W=0
```

### v-width-without-airway

- Severity: **warning**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [v-variable-assignment](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#v-variable-assignment)
- Automatic fix: no

V W= should only be used in an airspace with DY segments.

V W= sets the width of a DY airway. In an airspace without DY commands, the width has no effect. Remove it, or check that the airway is complete.

Correct:

```
V W=4
DY 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DY 46:00:00N 015:00:00E
```

Incorrect:

```
V W=4
DP 46:00:00N 014:00:00E
DP 46:00:00N 015:00:00E
DP 45:58:00N 015:00:00E
```

### v-center-unused

- Severity: **info**
- Versions: 2.1, 3.0
- Specification: [v-variable-assignment](https://github.com/naviter/seeyou_file_formats/blob/main/OpenAir_File_Format_Support.md#v-variable-assignment)
- Automatic fix: no

A V X= centre should be used by a DA, DB or DC command.

V X= sets the centre for the DA, DB and DC commands that follow it. If no such command follows before the next V X= or the end of the airspace, the centre has no effect. It is not an error, but it can mean that an arc or a circle is missing.

Correct:

```
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DC 2.00
```

Incorrect:

```
V X=50:35:36N 007:56:42E
DP 50:40:00N 007:56:42E
```
